title: Arjuna lays down his bow in grief

verses.sa: यद्यप्येते न पश्यन्ति लोभोपहतचेतसः । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं मित्रद्रोहे च पातकम् ॥
verses.tr: Though greed has blinded them, they do not see the fault in destroying a family or the wrong in betraying friends.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just said he would not kill his own kin. Here he explains why the other side does not see the harm they are causing. Listen for the reason they are blind.

body.text: Though greed has blinded them, they do not see the fault in destroying a family or the wrong in betraying friends. Listen to one phrase, lohopahata chetasa, blinded by greed. It is not that the Kauravas cannot see with their eyes; it is that greed has clouded their minds so they cannot see the fault in destroying a family or the sin in betraying friends. He asks why his own side should turn away from this sin, since they do see the fault in destroying the family.

verses.sa: कथं न ज्ञेयमस्माभिः पापादस्मान्निवर्तितुम् । कुलक्षयकृतं दोषं प्रपश्यद्भिर्जनार्दन ॥
verses.tr: Why should we not turn away from this sin, when we clearly see the fault in destroying the family, O Janardana?
verses.angle: Seeing the fault clearly is reason enough to turn back
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna sets aside his warrior's eagerness for victory. He sees that killing relatives will destroy the family, and he asks Krishna why they should step back.

body.text: Why should we not turn away from this sin, when we clearly see the fault in destroying the family, O Janardana? He does not wait for the other side to agree. He says that while they are blinded by greed, he and his side can clearly see the fault of destroying the family, and that alone is reason enough to turn away from this sin. He warns that once a family falls apart, its ancient duties are lost.

verses.sa: कुलक्षये प्रणश्यन्ति कुलधर्माः सनातनाः । धर्मे नष्टे कुलं कृत्स्नमधर्मोऽभिभवत्युत ॥
verses.tr: When a family falls apart, its ancient duties disappear. When duty is lost, wrongdoing overtakes the whole family.
verses.angle: kulam kritsnam, the entire family exposed
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna now traces what happens after the killing ends. Listen for the word that names the total ruin of the Kuru line.

body.text: When a family falls apart, its ancient duties disappear. When duty is lost, wrongdoing overtakes the whole family. The verse speaks of the entire family, kulam kritsnam. With the elders dead, nothing is left to hold the house together, and the whole line is left exposed to ruin. Arjuna says that this lawlessness then corrupts the women of the family, and from that corruption, social disorder is born.

verses.sa: अधर्माभिभवात्कृष्ण प्रदुष्यन्ति कुलस्त्रियः । स्त्रीषु दुष्टासु वार्ष्णेय जायते वर्णसङ्करः ॥
verses.tr: When lawlessness grows, the women of the family are corrupted. When women are corrupted, mixed social disorder is born.
verses.angle: Speaking to Krishna as Vrishni, Arjuna shows his trust
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just argued that a family in ruins loses its ancient duties. Now he looks ahead to the next generation. Listen to what he says will happen when lawlessness grows.

body.text: When lawlessness grows, the women of the family are corrupted. When women are corrupted, mixed social disorder is born. Arjuna names Krishna as his witness and calls him Vrishni, a descendant of his own family. By speaking to Krishna this way, he shows that he is laying out his deepest fear before the one person he trusts most. Arjuna then moves from the corruption of women to the ruin of lineage and the fall of ancestors.

verses.sa: सङ्करो नरकायैव कुलघ्नानां कुलस्य च । पतन्ति पितरो ह्येषां लुप्तपिण्डोदकक्रियाः ॥
verses.tr: Mixed lineage leads the destroyers of family to ruin, and their ancestors fall because offerings of food and water stop.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna now looks past the living to the dead, warning that civil war destroys the very rites that sustain the ancestors.

body.text: Mixed lineage leads the destroyers of family to ruin, and their ancestors fall because offerings of food and water stop. The word pitroh, ancestors, is followed by patanti, fall, meaning the dead themselves collapse from their place because the rites that feed them have stopped. Arjuna continues, stating that this mixed social disorder destroys the eternal duties of the family and community.

verses.sa: दोषैरेतैः कुलघ्नानां वर्णसङ्करकारकैः । उत्साद्यन्ते जातिधर्माः कुलधर्माश्च शाश्वताः ॥
verses.tr: Because of these faults that create mixed social order, the eternal duties of family and community are destroyed.
verses.angle: When conduct breaks, the inherited order that protects everyone breaks too.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna is building a chain of consequences for war. Listen for the final item on his list.

body.text: Because of these faults that create mixed social order, the eternal duties of family and community are destroyed. Arjuna calls his own side kulaghnanam, family-destroyers, and says that these faults destroy the eternal duties of family and community. He now says that those whose duties are destroyed dwell in a lower realm.

verses.sa: उत्सन्नकुलधर्माणां मनुष्याणां जनार्दन । नरकेऽनियतं वासो भवतीत्यनुशुश्रुम ॥
verses.tr: O Janardana, we have always heard that those whose family duties are destroyed dwell long in a lower realm.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna pauses his argument to cite an ancient teaching. Listen for the authority he relies on.

body.text: O Janardana, we have always heard that those whose family duties are destroyed dwell long in a lower realm. The word anushushruma means we have heard. Arjuna is not stating his own opinion here; he is leaning on a tradition he learned from his elders to justify his refusal to fight. He immediately follows by naming the grave wrong he has resolved to commit against his own kin.

verses.sa: अहो बत महत्पापं कर्तुं व्यवसिता वयम् । यद्राज्यसुखलोभेन हन्तुं स्वजनमुद्यताः ॥
verses.tr: Alas, we have resolved to commit a grave wrong, driven by greed for kingdom and pleasure, we are ready to kill our own kin.
verses.angle: vayum: the we that admits guilt
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna is no longer looking at the enemy. He is looking at his own side. Listen for the word that makes him own the guilt.

body.text: Alas, we have resolved to commit a grave wrong, driven by greed for kingdom and pleasure, we are ready to kill our own kin. Listen to one word, vayum, we. The verse says we are ready to kill our own kin, and he includes himself in that we. He is no longer just judging the other side. He now asks what good a kingdom will be if it is won by killing his own people.

verses.sa: यदि मामप्रतीकारमशस्त्रं शस्त्रपाणयः । धार्तराष्ट्रा रणे हन्युस्तन्मे क्षेमतरं भवेत् ॥
verses.tr: If the armed sons of Dhritarashtra were to kill me in battle while I stood unresisting and without weapons, that would be far better for me.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna looks at the armed Kaurava army and asks if it would be better to die unresisting than to raise his own weapon against his kin.

body.text: If the armed sons of Dhritarashtra were to kill me in battle while I stood unresisting and without weapons, that would be far better for me. Arjuna says it would be better to be killed unresisting and unarmed than to fight back against Dhritarashtra's sons, revealing his absolute refusal to defend himself. Sanjaya then reports that Arjuna sat down on the chariot, dropped his weapons, and gave way to grief.

verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वाऽर्जुनः संख्ये रथोपस्थ उपाविशत् । विसृज्य सशरं चापं शोकसंविग्नमानसः ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: Saying this, Arjuna sat down on the chariot seat in the midst of the battlefield, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief.
verses.angle: Casting aside the bow and arrows
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Arjuna has just spoken his despair. Sanjaya watches him drop his weapons and sink down. Listen to the weight of what he casts aside.

body.text: Sanjaya says: Saying this, Arjuna sat down on the chariot seat in the midst of the battlefield, casting aside his bow and arrows, his mind overwhelmed by grief. Arjuna casts aside his bow and arrows, his hands letting go of the very instruments of his duty, and he sits down in the middle of the battlefield. Sanjaya now turns to the moment when Krishna speaks to Arjuna, whose eyes are full of tears and clouded with grief.
